supporting_evidence: 37 column-level referential checks; 4 find any dangling value; 31,198 dangling ids total, of which 25,961 are explained by removed_* tombstones and 5,237 are not (term_concept_map.term_id rows tagged NOT_IN_TERMINOLOGY). Orphans: 1,092 datasets with no cohort/sample/assay; 9,940 terms with no mention; 93,604 with no mapping; 159,081 with no definition; 0 claims/relations without evidence; 0 papers without sections
limitation: The 5,237 are a sentinel population (a term id that deliberately does not exist, used to mark rows as not-in-terminology), so the referential picture is better than the raw figure suggests — but the sentinel is undocumented in the schema

measurable_indicator: stale rollups 11 / 14 = 78.6%
supporting_evidence: 14 rollups checked, 11 stale: canonical_term.mention_count disagrees on 61,839 / 152,333 = 40.59%; definition_count 3,316 / 162,409 = 2.04%; paper_count 11,756 / 152,333 = 7.72%; all six paper.n_* rollups disagree on 453 / 453 = 100%; relation.evidence_verified_count 12 rows. Three relation rollups are exactly consistent
limitation: The paper.n_* family is not staleness: component F proved they are mirrors of the catalogue clean layer (surplus 2,586 rows over 399/453 papers, n_findings +405). The canonical_term.mention_count staleness is genuine and unexplained

measurable_indicator: mention redundancy 45.6%; definition redundancy 6.3% (424/6,773)
supporting_evidence: term_mention: 2,505,684 rows → 1,362,888 distinct spans, i.e. 1,142,796 redundant rows (45.6%) by span collapse; canonical_term.term_norm 68 groups / 71 redundant; term_norm+cdm_type 2 / 2; surface near-duplicates 2,452 groups / 2,874 redundant (817 within type, 1,635 across); term_definition 272 / 424; term_concept_map 4,686 / 5,984; type_harmonization 363 / 447; relation 0 duplicate canonical triples
limitation: Span collapse means "the same section offsets were emitted by more than one model or more than once". It is expected in a multi-model table but it means term_mention is not a mention table, it is a mention-observation table

measurable_indicator: query reproduction 8 / 8 = 100%
supporting_evidence: All 8 / 8 published RESEARCH_QUERY_VALIDATION.csv queries run and reproduce their published row and paper counts exactly (Q1 35/35, Q2 63/18, Q3 103/58, Q4 771/442, Q5 24,272/451, Q6 60/60, Q7 603/191, Q8 101/101)
limitation: Reproduction is not correctness. Q7 is a confirmed defect: it filters storage_condition LIKE '%80%', which returns 80°C (ambient) as well as -80°C (frozen), because the minus glyph was destroyed upstream in 147 rows across 9 surfaces (component F, CQA-F-11). 25 papers depend on the defect; 62–70 of 453 papers contain sign-dropped 80 C/20 C text

measurable_indicator: missing research distinctions 3 / 3 probes negative; multi-value columns 183 / 866 = 21.1%
supporting_evidence: No diet field, no dose field, no effect-size field (all three probes negative); no sample-group table and no group column (sample_group_table_exists=false); sample.sample_count carries an aggregate-vs-per-row ambiguity the schema does not resolve; 183 semicolon multi-value columns; 59 JSON-encoded columns; 19 tables with no provenance column at all
limitation: The CDM cannot represent a diet intervention's composition, a dose, or an effect size with uncertainty — three things a microbiome intervention study always has. Multi-value columns store relations that the schema cannot express as relations

measurable_indicator: dictionary coverage 100%; change-log reversibility 79 / 79 rows carry revert_sql
supporting_evidence: Data dictionary covers 866 / 866 columns = 100.0%, 0 undocumented; a 79-row cdm_change_log with per-row revert_sql; run_metadata with 11 keys; MANIFEST.sha256 verifies 36 / 36 CDM files
limitation: The dictionary documents the columns, not their semantics: three status columns are constants (component G, CQA-G-09) and several columns carry sentinels the dictionary does not name

measurable_indicator: hash coverage 100% on sections and mentions; 0% on claim_evidence (claim_evidence_has_hash=false)
supporting_evidence: run_metadata: built 2026-10-31T12:19:10, migrated 2026-11-02T02:12:44, promoted 2026-11-02T08:04:46 from 3.0.3-rc1; 5/5 upstream file hashes MATCH; section.text_hash_sha256 on 4,006/4,006 sections and term_mention.section_text_sha256 on 2,505,684/2,505,684 mentions
limitation: The build is traceable to inputs, but not re-executable: no DDL script ships with the bundle, so the schema cannot be recreated from the release alone

measurable_indicator: index coverage: 39/44 tables have ≥1 index; 5 have none; term_mention indexes are single-column only
supporting_evidence: term_mention (2.5 M rows) has no composite (paper, section, offset) index; any span self-join is quadratic and killed job 28697992
limitation: Performance is a usability property, not a correctness one — but on this dataset it decides whether an analysis is feasible

measurable_indicator: identical splits: yes (500 / 100 abstracts); chance-corrected comparisons present; in-domain advantage flagged
supporting_evidence: All models scored on the same official splits with whole title+abstract; exact and relaxed matching both reported; full-schema F1 counts types a model cannot emit as misses and n/a cells are shown explicitly; in-domain training flagged †; document-bootstrap 95% CIs and permutation p-values reported for every row
limitation: The comparison mixes kinds: a curated database lookup (PubTator3), trained token classifiers, zero-shot NER, and 3-shot LLMs sit in one ranked table. That is a legitimate "what is available" comparison but not a controlled model comparison — and the winner is the one that is not a model run

measurable_indicator: every headline number carries an interval; every pairwise claim carries a p-value
supporting_evidence: 95% CI by document bootstrap on every F1; significance vs the best row (p vs best); Wilson intervals on every proportion; bootstrap intervals on every rate; permutation tests in the per-model evaluation
limitation: Bootstrap over 500/100 documents is wide for the smaller corpus (BioRED n=100), so small rank differences there are not resolvable — and the report says so via CI overlap (PubTator3 78.3 [71.2–85.0] vs HunFlair2 80.6 [78.3–82.8], p=0.274)

measurable_indicator: checksummed artefacts 0 / 3 at the time of audit [superseded: manifest 1 / 3, retrospective; prompt bundle recovered; preregistration still absent]; 54 unhashed prediction files [superseded: 126 files / ≈3.57 GB sealed]
supporting_evidence: 54 prediction files exist in preds/, the metrics JSON is complete, and the protocol is named (src/scripts/ner_fair_bench/fairbench.py) — but the directory contains no MANIFEST.sha256 and no PREREGISTRATION.sha256 [superseded in part — a dated retrospective seal now exists, and the prompts were recovered and verified; preregistration is still absent. See NER_BENCHMARK_CORRECTIONS.md §5–6 and NER_REPRODUCIBILITY_GAPS.md]
limitation: Revised upward because all 1,186 reported values were recomputed from the predictions with 0 mismatches, checkpoint revisions were recovered from job logs, and a seal now exists. Still not STRONG: there is no preregistration, run-time library versions are unrecorded, and the LLM prediction files discard off-schema entities before writing

dimension: Coverage of the CDM's own types
measurable_indicator: target-type coverage 2/14 on BC5CDR, 6/14 on BioRED, 0 benchmarks for the five microbiome-specific types [superseded: those are counts of benchmark types present, not CDM types covered; wholly unbenchmarked CDM types = 9, not 6 — §1.4 of the correction]
supporting_evidence: BC5CDR covers 2 types (Chemical, Disease); BioRED covers 6 (Chemical, Disease, Gene, Variant, CellLine, Species). The CDM vocabulary is 14 types, and the dominant extracted type is ENTITY (89,799 terms, 55.29%) with ORGANISM second (component C). No benchmark in the suite tests ORGANISM, MICROBIOME, LAB_METHOD, DATA_ANALYSIS, DIET, or HABITAT — the types that carry the corpus's scientific content [superseded: ORGANISM is approximated by BioRED OrganismTaxon; MICROBIOME/DIET/HABITAT are not CDM types. Correct split: 2 direct / 3 approximate / 9 none. See NER_TYPE_COVERAGE_MATRIX.csv]
limitation: The benchmark can rank extractors on chemical/disease mention finding. It cannot tell you whether any extractor finds a taxon, a method, or a body site correctly, which is what the CDM is for

measurable_indicator: max grounding 41.3%; median far lower; CellLine 0% for every configuration
supporting_evidence: 25 configurations carry a grounding block over 21.56 M chars / 7,161 chunks (scispacy_lg is untyped and carries none); per-type grounding reported against external reference lexicons, not the CDM vocabulary [corrected 2026-11-05 — see §6a]. Best chemical grounding 41.3% (bert_chemical, 1,702/4,123 unique), scispacy_craft 38.1%, bert_disease 29.2%, scispacy_bc5cdr 25.7%, llm_gemma_zs OrganismTaxon 25.3%; 0.0% for CellLine across all models
limitation: [superseded — the circularity claim below is wrong] Grounding is measured against external lexicons (NCBI Gene, CTD/MEDIC, Mondo, HPO, NCBI Taxonomy, OMOP), not the project's own term layer, so it is not circular; it remains a precision proxy (a string can hit an unrelated synonym, a real entity can be absent). The CellLine 0% is definitional — ground() returns set() for that type. See correction §9

measurable_indicator: KG support 36.5% of 137 grounded microbe–disease edges; 0/8 gene–disease
supporting_evidence: corpus_metrics.json:cdm_triples: microbe–disease 943 triples, 137 with both ends grounded, 50 KG-supported = 36.5% of grounded; gene–disease 29 triples / 8 grounded / 0 supported; chem–disease and chem–gene 0 triples.
limitation: Support is a coverage statement about a reference KG (component L). A 36.5% figure over 137 edges is a very small denominator and must not be read as precision.

measurable_indicator: per-config type breakdown present; explicit measurement notes present
supporting_evidence: ner_quality_quantity_2026-11-03/ compares volume against the merged metrics and the type table (per_config_type.csv); the report carries MEASUREMENT_NOTES.md documenting what was and was not measured
limitation: Volume is easy to inflate: the highest-row configuration is not the best one, and the corpus layer later collapses 45.6% duplicate spans (component H, CQA-H-06) — a benchmark that ranks by rows would reward redundancy

measurable_indicator: "best model" changes with corpus (pubtator3 on BC5CDR, hunflair2 on BioRED) and the top BC5CDR entry is not deployable for full-text section NER (PubTator3 is excluded from section mode in the pipeline)
supporting_evidence: The ranked table's top row is pubtator3 † (BC5CDR 90.1 [88.4–91.6]) — a precomputed API result trained on BC5CDR, i.e. an in-domain curated database lookup, not a model the project can run on its own corpus. The best runnable general models are hunflair2 † 77.3 and llm_qwen_fs 69.5. On BioRED the order flips: hunflair2 80.6 > pubtator3 78.3 (p=0.274)
limitation: A reader skimming the table will conclude "use PubTator3". The pipeline itself cannot, for section-level work, and the manuscript must not recommend a component it does not run

measurable_indicator: throughput spread ≈560× between fastest and slowest; same 7,161 chunks / 21.56 M chars for all
supporting_evidence: s/doc reported per configuration (0.0116 s for bert_chemical to 6.53 s for llm_llama_zs), device recorded per model (A40 GPU, CPU (8 cores)), chunk and char counts fixed across models
limitation: Total GPU-hours are not aggregated, so the cost of the chosen configuration is not stated as a single number

measurable_indicator: reversibility 100% — the input can be reconstructed row-for-row, and every changed field has its original beside it
supporting_evidence: Frozen CDM unmodified (all audits open mode=ro); every cleaned row carries relation_original, type_original, kept, drop_reason; MANIFEST.sha256 verifies 4/4 files; relabel.jsonl records each relabel
limitation: Recoverability is structural, not semantic: you can get the old value back, but you cannot recover the reason for each of 6,203 relabels beyond sentence / triple_only

measurable_indicator: generator script absent; rubric/prompt absent; model version named only in the output directory
supporting_evidence: Artefacts are checksummed and the judge run is named (llm_judge_deepseek_v4_flash), but no builder script ships in the repository — src/scripts/kg/ contains only build_kg.py, evidence_check.py, gold_kg_check.py, all of which consume the cleaned layer; a repository-wide search finds no generator
limitation: The transformation cannot be re-run from the release. The judge's rubric is not shipped either, so the keep/drop rule is documented only by CLEANING_REPORT.md prose

measurable_indicator: not-well-formed share 60.7%; invalid-entity share 1.73%; survivor share 37.5%
supporting_evidence: Dropped 16,106: not_well_formed 15,661 (60.7% of all triples) + invalid_entities 445. Kept 9,682. The 15,661 include strings like 100lofathp1cellsuspension106cellsml — concatenated PDF artefacts (see removed_relation samples in component G)
limitation: "Not well formed" is a model judgment against an unshipped rubric. That 60.7% of the frozen graph is judged ill-formed is a finding about the frozen graph, and it is the single largest claim in the layer

measurable_indicator: generic share 67.9% → 4.5% within the kept set; invented vocabulary 0
supporting_evidence: Among the 9,682 kept, OTHER_RELATION falls from 6,574 (67.9%) to 437 (4.5%); 6,146 of the 6,203 relabels start from OTHER_RELATION; 0 new relation labels are introduced — every target already exists in the frozen 76-relation vocabulary
limitation: The improvement is real inside the kept set, but the kept set is 37.5% of the graph, so the end-to-end generic share across the whole frozen population only falls from 68.7% to 1.7% of the original. Quoting 4.5% without the denominator misleads

measurable_indicator: relabels without sentence evidence 38.8%; swaps 408 (1.6% of all rows, 4.2% of kept)
supporting_evidence: Of 6,203 relabels, evidence is sentence for 3,796 (61.2%) and triple_only for 2,407 (38.8%) — i.e. two in five relabels have no sentence-level support recorded. Among generic→typed relabels specifically: sentence 3,895 / triple_only 2,638 / none 41. direction_swapped=1 on 408 (299 sentence, 109 triple_only)
limitation: A triple_only relabel is the model reading subject — OTHER_RELATION — object and choosing a predicate from the pair alone. That is exactly the regime where a plausible-sounding but unsupported predicate is produced. No human checked any of them

measurable_indicator: drop rate 81.1%; retype rate 37.8% of kept; ENTITY collapse −90.4%
supporting_evidence: 131,682 of 162,409 terms (81.1%) dropped; 30,727 kept; 11,614 retyped; ENTITY falls 7,735 → 744 among kept. The drop rule is internally consistent: 0 dropped terms have valid_mention_share ≥ 0.5
limitation: An 81% term drop is an enormous claim and it is model-generated. valid_mention_share is computed from the same judge, so the consistency check above is circular by construction, not independent confirmation

measurable_indicator: off-vocabulary ENTITY among kept 7,735 → 744 (−90.4%); all target labels are in the 14-type CDM vocabulary
supporting_evidence: The cleaned vocabulary is drawn entirely from CDM_TYPES — ORGANISM 5,485 / CHEMICAL 4,735 / DATA_ANALYSIS 4,170 / DISEASE 3,279 / LAB_METHOD 2,338 / PROTEIN 2,155 / CLINICAL 1,788 / DNA_RNA 1,662 — and removes the off-vocabulary ENTITY label from 6,991 of 7,735 kept terms
limitation: Moving to CDM_TYPES fixes a vocabulary defect (component C) but says nothing about whether each individual re-type is right; 11,614 were changed with no gold standard

measurable_indicator: node attrition 60.6%; component count −60.1%; largest-component share essentially unchanged (68.5% → 67.8%)
supporting_evidence: Kept graph: 8,897 nodes / 9,682 edges / 1,219 components / largest 6,029 (67.8%) / 2 isolated / mean degree 2.11. Full graph: 22,579 nodes / 3,052 components / largest 15,470 (68.5%) / 73 isolated. 13,682 nodes (60.6%) are orphaned by the cleaning
limitation: Cleaning removes volume without changing the graph's topology: it is still one dominant blob. That is evidence the layer is pruning, not restructuring

measurable_indicator: unverifiable transformations 14,021 of 30,727 terms + 9,682 triples touched (retype 11,614 + no-evidence relabel 2,407)
supporting_evidence: New relation labels: 0. New term types: 0 (all in CDM_TYPES). But 2,407 relabels and 109 swaps have no sentence evidence; 11,614 re-types and 1,614 sentence-evidenced relabels are unverified; drop_reason is a single model's label with no second opinion
limitation: Nothing is overwritten — the original survives beside it — so the risk is not loss, it is a reader mistaking the cleaned value for a verified one

measurable_indicator: kept-vs-dropped deltas +10.0 pts (BugSigDB), +9.0 pts (KG, microbe–disease), +13.5 pts (evidence check)
supporting_evidence: Independent corroboration from component G/L: kept triples are better KG-supported (15.45% vs 6.41%, microbe–disease) and better evidence-supported (30.65% vs 17.15%); BugSigDB: kept 54.3% vs dropped 44.3% (+10.0 pts, CI 1.1–18.6). Direction agreement 91.7% (11/12)
limitation: All three corroborations are external and independent of the DeepSeek judge, which is what makes the layer's selection credible even though its labels are not verified

measurable_indicator: match coverage 47 / 453 = 10.4% of the corpus; identifier basis 98.5% PMID
supporting_evidence: 47 of 453 papers matched: PMID 266 + DOI 4 = 270 matched on PMID alone, 4 additional on DOI. BugSigDB export is versioned and dated, and the licence (CC BY 4.0) is recorded in the artefact
limitation: PMID matching is exact and auditable. The 10.4% is not a matching failure — BugSigDB has curated only 47 of these papers — but it does bound what the comparison can say about the rest

measurable_indicator: reference provenance complete (source, version, licence, protocol, code hash)
supporting_evidence: Export timestamped to the minute, licence stated, scoring_schema.json named as the protocol, item-level records written, code_sha256 recorded, all verdicts enumerated
limitation: No MANIFEST.sha256 for this directory, so the item file itself is unhashed — a small gap in an otherwise clean provenance chain

measurable_indicator: coverage 27.72% vs 8.97% chance = 3.1×; exact coverage 23.49%
supporting_evidence: 1,537 BugSigDB taxa items; 361 MATCH + 65 PARTIAL, 1,111 MISMATCH → coverage 27.72% (Wilson 25.54–30.01; paper bootstrap 21.53–35.84); chance 8.97%, chance-corrected 20.6%; exact (not genus-collapsed) coverage 23.49%
limitation: "Coverage" is the share of BugSigDB's curated taxa that our extraction also reports. It is a recall-like quantity only for the subset BugSigDB curates — i.e. signature taxa in 47 papers. It says nothing about the other 406 papers, and nothing about taxa BugSigDB did not record

measurable_indicator: support 57.27% vs 18.1% chance = 3.2×
supporting_evidence: 667 of our taxa items in those papers: MATCH 361 + PARTIAL 21, NOT_IN_REFERENCE 285 → support 57.27% (53.49–60.97; bootstrap 48.04–67.09); chance 18.1%
limitation: Support is "of the taxa we report in these papers, how many BugSigDB also lists". It is precision-like only against BugSigDB's scope: a correct taxon that is not a differential-abundance signature is counted NOT_IN_REFERENCE

measurable_indicator: direction agreement 77.0% vs 52.0% post-hoc chance on 261 items
supporting_evidence: Of 667 items, 261 determinable (165 UNDETERMINED): SAME 201, OPPOSITE 60 → 77.01% same (71.54–81.70; bootstrap 66.36–86.45); post-hoc chance 51.96%
limitation: 60 opposite-direction calls is a substantial minority and is not broken out by taxon, body site or condition, so the audit cannot say whether they concentrate anywhere. The 165 UNDETERMINED (24.7%) are silently outside the rate

measurable_indicator: strong: sequencing_type, platform, region_16s, country, condition (0.94–1.00); weak: body_site 0.246, group_name 0.542, group_size 0.563
supporting_evidence: Nine fields compared against BugSigDB, each with completeness, concordance, Wilson CI, bootstrap CI and a chance baseline: sequencing_type 48/1.000 (chance 0.962), region_16s 45/0.977 (0.348), platform 47/1.000 (0.939), country 50/0.940 (0.212), condition 55/0.927 (0.050), statistical_test 58/0.857 (0.440), group_size 176/0.5625 (0.063), group_name 249/0.5422 (0.050), body_site 57/0.2456 (0.050)
limitation: Several "strong" fields have chance baselines near 0.95 (sequencing_type 0.962, platform 0.939), so 1.000 is close to no information — the corpus is overwhelmingly 16S on Illumina, and agreement is the base rate. Only condition (0.927 vs 0.05) and country (0.94 vs 0.21) are genuinely informative

measurable_indicator: CI on 100% of reported rates; post-hoc labelling 100%
supporting_evidence: Wilson interval + paper-level bootstrap on every rate; chance baseline for every field; chance-corrected values; post-hoc analyses explicitly labelled (posthoc_direction_chance, posthoc_strict_set_equal, posthoc_coverage_by_source)
limitation: The post-hoc direction chance of 51.96% is computed after seeing the data and is labelled as such — correct practice, but it means the 77%-vs-52% contrast is not a pre-registered test

measurable_indicator: adjudicated items 0 / 2,989 = 0.00%
supporting_evidence: Every field carries "adjudication": {} — empty in all nine. There is no second curator, no disagreement resolution, no spot-check. Taxa verdicts (MATCH/PARTIAL/MISMATCH) are rule-produced; nothing was human-confirmed
limitation: The protocol has an adjudication slot and it was never used, which is honest but leaves the whole comparison single-instrument. Where a rule mis-parses a taxon name, no reviewer catches it

measurable_indicator: snapshot staleness 8 / 668 = 1.2% of overlapping taxa; 71 / 8,479 = 0.84% of the full dump
supporting_evidence: Taxonomy snapshot 2026-11-01; BugSigDB overlap 668 distinct taxa, 8 absent from the snapshot (e.g. 1532, 81850, 155615, 424536), 660 with a name, 0 name differences from current; full BugSigDB dump 8,479 taxa, 71 absent from the snapshot
limitation: The comparison is against a snapshot two days older than the export, which is negligible. The "our ontologies are newer" question is answered here by measurement, not assertion: 0 name differences, 8 missing ids

measurable_indicator: corpus coverage 10.4% of papers
supporting_evidence: 47 / 453 papers = 10.4%; 667 of our taxa items; 261 determinable directions. Post-hoc coverage by BugSigDB source shows the comparison is dominated by figures (754 items, 27.6%) and supplements (660, 22.1%), with tables (105, 51.4%) and text (18, 100%) far smaller
limitation: The 47 papers are not a random sample — they are the papers BugSigDB chose to curate, which skews toward well-known, well-studied studies. A 57% support rate on that subset is plausibly the best case in the corpus

measurable_indicator: pre-registered 2 / 2 runs; code hash 2 / 2
supporting_evidence: Both runs ship PREREGISTRATION.sha256; the Nov-3 protocol is named (scoring_schema.json v1.0), item schema validated, code_sha256 recorded; the Nov-4 run carries code_sha256 and a schema file (gold_kg_schema.json)
limitation: The thresholds (what counts as MATCH vs PARTIAL) were fixed before scoring, which is what makes the negative CTD result credible rather than a fishing expedition

measurable_indicator: manifest verification 100% (4/4); unlisted files 0
supporting_evidence: Nov-3: MANIFEST.sha256 4/4 verified, 0 mismatch, 0 missing, 0 unlisted; item-level items.jsonl; Nov-4: PREREGISTRATION.sha256 + manifest
limitation: The Nov-4 run's edges.csv.gz is large but hashed; the reference snapshots themselves (BugSigDB/CTD/Disbiome dumps) are dated but not bundled

measurable_indicator: support 50.4% vs 16.1% chance = 3.1×; kept−dropped +10.0 pts, CI excludes 0
supporting_evidence: 518 items on 45 of 47 overlap papers: MATCH 242 + PARTIAL 19 = 50.4% (261/518; 46.1–54.7), paper bootstrap 42.1–58.8; chance 16.1%; kept 54.3% (172/317) vs dropped 44.3% (89/201); kept−dropped +10.0 pts (1.1–18.6)
limitation: Taxon resolution is name_match on 401/518 and cdm_mapping on 117/518 — so 77% of the links rest on string matching, and a name match does not establish that the same taxon is meant (strain-level differences, renamed genera)

measurable_indicator: any support 22.4% vs 24.2% chance = null; curated 8.2% vs 2.1% chance = 3.9× on 4 items
supporting_evidence: 49 items: CURATED 4 / NOT_IN_REFERENCE 38 / INFERRED_ONLY 7. Any support 22.4% (11/49; 13.0–35.9) vs chance 24.2% — at or below chance. Curated support 8.2% (4/49; 3.2–19.2) vs chance 2.1%. Kept 22.2% (8/36) vs dropped 23.1% (3/13); kept−dropped −0.9 pts (−30.0 to +20.9)
limitation: The two readings point in opposite directions and both are published. The honest summary is "no evidence of enrichment at the any-support level; a 4-item curated signal that cannot be distinguished from noise"

measurable_indicator: support 0/7; interval spans zero to 35%
supporting_evidence: 7 items, all NOT_IN_REFERENCE; 0/7 (CI −0.0 to 35.4); chance 0.0; kept 0/4, dropped 0/3
limitation: With n=7 and a zero chance baseline, this is a null result that carries no information either way — and it should be labelled as such rather than reported as a failure

measurable_indicator: direction 91.7% on n=12
supporting_evidence: Taxon-as-subject, directional relation, determinable: same direction 11/12 = 91.7% (64.6–98.5) vs base-rate chance 50.0%; same kept pairs original vs cleaned relation, n=7: 85.7% both
limitation: n=12. The interval (64.6–98.5) is compatible with a true rate anywhere from "barely better than a coin" to "almost always right"

measurable_indicator: overlapping headline numbers not comparable: 50.4% (Nov-3, 518 items) vs 13.18% (Nov-4, 622 edges)
supporting_evidence: The two runs disagree on the reference set and the denominator: Nov-3 uses BugSigDB + CTD (518 items, Disbiome absent); Nov-4 uses BugSigDB + Disbiome (59 supports) + CTD on 622 resolved edges with microbe–disease support 13.18% vs 5.78% chance. Same question, different populations, different reference sets, different denominators
limitation: Both are defensible individually. Presented together without reconciliation, a reader will see two "BugSigDB support" figures that differ by a factor of four. The difference is the denominator (items vs resolved edges) and the reference set — not a contradiction, but it reads as one

measurable_indicator: graph coverage 847 / 25,788 = 3.28%; name_match+name_only 289 of 622 microbe–disease edges (46.5%)
supporting_evidence: 518 + 49 + 7 = 574 checked items; the Nov-4 run resolves 847 edges of 25,788 = 3.28%. The remaining 96.7% are untested because their ends never resolved to an identifier
limitation: Coverage is limited by resolution, and resolution is limited by the absent ontology layer (component G, CQA-G-01). The reference check inherits that defect

measurable_indicator: scope violations 0
supporting_evidence: The Nov-3 report's own line: "Support by a reference, not accuracy: a triple absent from BugSigDB or CTD is not counted as wrong, and CTD support shows that an association is known, not that the paper stated it." The Nov-4 tier statement: "KG support is a coverage statement; a triple absent from the KG is untested, not incorrect." A scope scan of the Tier-3 report finds 0 occurrences of accuracy/recall/F1/precision/gold_standard/agreement
limitation: This is the component that most often goes wrong in biomedical KG papers, and here the wording is correct in both runs. It should be preserved verbatim in the manuscript

measurable_indicator: verification rate 100% (299/299); unlisted 1, benign
supporting_evidence: 299 / 299 manifest entries verify; 0 mismatches; 0 missing; 0 unlisted artefacts except MANIFEST.sha256 itself, which cannot hash itself and is the correct exception. manifest_problems is empty
limitation: The manifest covers the bundle it ships with, so it proves integrity in transit, not integrity of the build

measurable_indicator: count reproduction 7 / 7 = 100%
